paragraphs: Abaye bar Avin, [Berakhot 29b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.9); Rav Ada bar Avin, [Keritot 21a:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.21a.10); Rav Achadvoi bar Avin, [Avodah Zarah 34b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.34b.13) according to the Dikdukei Soferim reading; Rav Idi bar Avin, [Berakhot 14a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.14a.16); Rav Ika, [Keritot 20a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.20a.11), while [Shabbat 20b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.20b.15) reads Rami ba Avin; Rav Ashi bar Avin, [Shabbat 66b:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66b.7); Rav Huna bar Avin, [Rosh Hashanah 21a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.21a.8); R’ Huna the Priest bar Avin, Midrash Tehillim 110:3; Rav Chiyya bar Avin, [Berakhot 27b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.27b.9); R’ Chanina bar Avin, [Berakhot 29b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.9); R’ Yehoshua bar Avin, [Ruth Rabbah 2:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Ruth_Rabbah.2.10) [supplied locator: פ״נ־ו]; R’ Yose bar Avin, [Berakhot 13a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.13a.13); R’ Yaakov bar Avin, Vayikra Rabbah 20:11; R’ Yitzchak bar Avin, Rosh Hashanah 19a; Marion son of Ravin, [Moed Katan 11b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.11b.12); Rav Natan bar Avin, [Chullin 45b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.45b.15); Rav bar Avin, [Pesachim 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.40a.8).[^4][^5][^6]

notes.text: This is a collective list. The abbreviation bar Avin follows the heading and repeated full patronymics; it does not assert one shared father. The Ruth Rabbah label פ״נ־ו remains irregular.

No new whole primary scalar was returned. The earlier Yalkut Ruth 601 search snippet is a lead only, not a whole named witness for Hyman’s irregular Ruth Rabbah locator פ״נ־ו. The earlier bounded Ruth Rabbah 2 no-match is not a global absence claim. Midrash Tehillim פ״קי-ג gives 110:3 as the supplied numerical reading, replacing the older mistaken 80:13 gloss without a fresh passage verification. This collection preserves eighteen listed name/report forms, not one father: Abaye and Rami are untitled, Ika has no supplied patronymic, Rami ba Avin is not silently repaired to bar Avin, and Marion is son of Ravin without turning Ravin into a title. All nine explicit full Rav occurrences remain full; Huna the Priest, Chanina, Yehoshua, Yose, Yaakov and Yitzchak have abbreviated titles and remain R-prime. The other b-A patronymic expansions follow the repeated local bar Avin forms only; no identity merge or duplicate retirement is made. All source holds remain.

The checked printed Hyman entry (vol. I, p. 89) lists Rav Ika bar Avin at Megillah 3a and R’ Ami bar Avin at Keritot 20a separately. Both consulted passages support that distinction. The supplied Hebrew contracts the two entries and reads Rami ba Avin, where the print and the consulted Shabbat 20b read Rami bar Avin. The consulted Berakhot 27b has Rabbi Chiyya, and Pesachim 40a has the household of Rava bar Avin. Ruth Rabbah 2:10 names Yehoshua berabbi Avin, while Yalkut Shimoni on Ruth 601:1 reads Yehoshua bar Avin. A reproduced Hebrew text of Midrash Tehillim 110:3 names Huna the Priest bar Avin speaking in Bivi’s name. The consulted OYW chapter text instead names Yehudah the Priest bar Avin. The consulted Avodah Zarah 34b gives Achadvoi without the patronymic. The Dikdukei Soferim reading remains Hyman’s citation. The consulted Rosh Hashanah 19a–b text did not confirm the supplied Yitzchak bar Avin attribution.

Megillah gives Rav Ika bar Avin, Keritot gives Ami and Chananya bar Avin, and Shabbat gives Rami bar Avin. The two linked Ruth witnesses give Yehoshua berabbi Avin and Yehoshua bar Avin respectively. Pesachim names the household of Rava bar Avin. These forms have distinct textual settings. See also [Megillah 3a (Rav Ika bar Avin)](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.3a.7), [Keritot 20a (Ami and Chananya bar Avin)](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.20a.11), [Yalkut Shimoni on Ruth, remez 601](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.601.1).

[Berakhot 29b:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.29b.9) names Abaye and Rabbi Chanina with the same patronymic. The Davidson translation describes them as brothers. Hyman’s wider list includes other bearers of the name. In [Keritot 20a:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.20a.11), Ami and Rav Chananya introduce the explanation that continues at [Keritot 20b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.20b.1). In [Berakhot 13a:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.13a.13), Rabbi Yose bar Avin and Rabbi Yose bar Zevida are alternative attributions of the same objection.
[Rosh Hashanah 17a:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.17a.6) names Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avin in the comparison to the bottom of a pot. Hyman cites Rosh Hashanah 19a.
